messages:
anna: @channel seeing a sharp p99/timeouts spike right after the 12:30 deploy. dashboards show p95 ~120ms -> 600ms, p99 jumping to 2.3s and a rising 502/504 count. tagging oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT opened: timeout-regression (priority: P1). Pager duty: paging oncall. link: https://telemetry.redwood/graph/abc123
pagerduty-bot: @anna -> oncall paged (raj). ETA acknowledging.
raj: I'm awake, looking now. can everyone drop non-essential noise (no deploys, no infra changes)
jeff: curious if this is multiplex or gateway. telemetry shows a spike of gateway timeouts between frontend and runtime. 5xx mostly 502s from runtime pool.
sophie: rolling windows show KV cache miss rate up ~30% at the same time as deploy. could be kv-affinity change in latest runtime.
raj: can we confirm which revision rolled? build id: rwd-runtime@2026-03-15-315. config diff shows new connection pooling change and kvcache sharding tweak.
anna: logs from runtime nodes show a lot of 'connection reset by peer' and retries on the grpc layer. paste: ```Mar 15 12:30:12 runtime-23 runtime[pid]: WARN grpc: conn reset, retried=3 target=kv-proxy cluster=pool-7```
jeff: re-run perf test against canary image locally — reproduces p99 bump when kvcache misses and many simultaneous cold starts. suspect sticky KV affinity logic causing hot sharding leading to queues and eventual 502s.
raj: mitigation plan: 1) stop rollout (pause canaries), 2) scale runtime pool up by +20% to buy headroom, 3) gate kvcache sharding feature off (feature flag), 4) if that doesn't help, roll back to previous runtime. who can flip flag?
sophie: ops can flip. I'm preparing the flag command. ops: please stand by.
ops: running: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/flags/rollback -d '{"flag":"kvcache_shard_v2","value":false}'` -> response 200 OK. Rolling out flag to region-us-east-1.
raj: flipping looks applied to 12/15 hosts, still pending on autoscaler pods. watching metrics.
jeff: p95 improved to ~180ms, p99 coming down to ~800ms, 502s dropping. good sign.
anna: customer impact: some real-time customers saw retries and elevated latency around 12:30-12:45. SLO error budget hit for a small subset of dedicated customers. we'll need outreach if they hit client-side deadlines.
incident-bot: Update: severity remains P1 until stabilized for 30m.
raj: I'm going to scale the runtime pool +25% to drain queued requests. `kubectl scale deployment runtime --replicas=50 -n prod`. Doing now.
ops: scale complete. nodes coming up healthy. latency continues to trend down.
sophie: can we avoid a full rollback? flag flip + scale seems to be working. but the safe path is rollback since change is risky. decision needed: rollback to rwd-runtime@2026-03-10-301?
jeff: my call — patched flag + scale looks stable with p99 ~200-300ms. I recommend holding rollback and continue monitoring for 30min.
raj: agreed. I'll keep watch and set a rollback timer at +30m if p99 > 500ms or 5xx rate > 0.5%.
anna: I'll draft customer impact notes and a short incident timeline for outreach. tagging @sophie for root-cause followups.
ops: note — we saw a pod drain error on runtime-17: `error draining connections: stuck 120s`. adding to RCA items.
jeff: thanks. let's also capture traces for a few affected requests (trace ids: 00-abc-1, 00-def-2).
raj: marking mitigations: feature flag off, runtime scale up. leaving the deploy paused. scheduling a handoff to night oncall at 13:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Hand-off scheduled to night-oncall at 2026-03-15T13:00:00Z.
anna: final note: no rollback executed. will update if anything changes. postmortem owner: sophie. action items: revert sticky-affinity change until we have load-tested rollout, add automatic canary rollback threshold for KV miss spikes, improve draining logic to fail fast and fallback.
ops: closing channel for non-essential chatter. thumbs if you ack. :thumbsup:
raj: ack.
jeff: ack.
sophie: ack.
anna: ack.
incident-bot: INCIDENT status: mitigated, monitoring. will auto-close after 60m of stable metrics.
